newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 GDP growth very encouraging--spokesman.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 GDP growth very encouraging--spokesman.

text.p: Initial estimates of growth in India's gross domestic product (GDP) in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31 are "very, very encouraging", a government spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman told Reuters by telephone that the government was trying to spur growth in all sectors of the economy, not just the capital market.
"On a very broad front, GDP has really picked up. Growth this year is very, very encouraging," the spokesman said. He declined to disclose the official GDP growth estimate for 1996/97.
In 1995/96, real GDP, adjusted for inflation, rose by 7.1 percent after 7.2 percent a year earlier.
The spokesman was asked if the government, as widely expected in the financial capital Bombay, would announce a package of measures this week to shore up the capital market.
"The capital market is an important segment. The government effort is to move on a very broad front so the economy picks up in all sectors, not just the capital market," he said.
